title: Chat basics
text: A conversation is the unit chat is organized into: a list of messages between you and one or more participants (the default assistant, or an agent you have added). Conversations belong to a project, not to you personally — a conversation started in a shared project is visible to anyone with access to that project, the same as any other project resource. Starting a new conversation Open Chat and either continue the most recent conversation in the current project or start a new one. Each conversation keeps its own message history and its own set of attached context. Adding an agent to a conversation Optional An agent is an assistant configured with a specific prompt, model, and set of tools. Add one as a participant to route messages to it instead of (or alongside) the default assistant. A conversation can have more than one agent participant at once — each message still goes to whichever participant you address it to. Sharing a conversation A share link makes one conversation readable by anyone who has the link, with no sign in required. The recipient sees the messages as they existed when the link was generated; they cannot post new messages or see other conversations in the project. Anyone with a share link can read that conversation for as long as the link stays valid — treat it like any other link to information you would not want indexed publicly. See Quick start for signing in before you get to a conversation at all.

title: Welcome to Elitea
text: Elitea is a workspace for building and running AI agents, pipelines, and chat based assistants on top of your own data and tools. This is a placeholder page: it exercises the docs SPA's navigation, search, and component contract while the content team ports the real guide pages over from the previous documentation site. title: Quick start
text: This walks through the shortest path from an invite to a working conversation. You need an invite or an account created by your organization's admin — Elitea does not have open self signup. Sign in Go to your organization's Elitea URL and choose your identity provider on the sign in screen. Elitea provisions a personal project for every user on first sign in — it is where your own chats, agents, and credentials live before you share anything with a team project. Open Chat and type a message. The default model responds using whatever provider your project has configured. Choose how you connect The web app at your organization's Elitea URL. This is what most people mean by "Elitea" day to day. The same platform over its /llm OpenAI compatible endpoint, for scripts and integrations that need programmatic access rather than a chat window. An API key inherits the permissions of the project it was issued under. Treat it like a password: it is not tied to your browser session and does not expire when you sign out. Frequently asked Yes, provided a project admin has added your provider's credentials under that project's settings. See Toolkits overview for how external connections are configured more generally. A share link opens the conversation read only for anyone who has it, with no sign in required — see Chat basics.

title: Toolkits overview
text: A toolkit gives an agent a set of callable tools backed by an external service — a code repository, a project tracker, a documentation source. An agent with a toolkit attached can read from (and, where the toolkit allows it, write to) that service as part of answering a message. Adding a toolkit to a project 1. Open the project's Toolkits settings. 2. Choose a toolkit and provide the credentials it asks for (an API token, a base URL, or both, depending on the service). 3. Attach the configured toolkit to an agent so its tools appear in that agent's tool list. Credentials are stored once per project and can be reused by every toolkit and agent in that project — you do not re enter them per agent. What a toolkit exposes | Category | Examples | Typical use | | | | | | Code repositories | source hosting, pull requests | reading and proposing code changes | | Project management | issue trackers | reading and filing issues | | Documentation | wikis, knowledge bases | answering from indexed docs | A toolkit's tools run with the credentials configured for the project, not the credentials of whoever is chatting — a member of the project can trigger any action the toolkit's stored credential is allowed to perform. Continue with Chat basics to see how an agent with a toolkit attached behaves inside a conversation, or back to Quick start if you have not signed in yet.
